courses.title: Current Topics in Clinical Practice I, II
courses.description: Presentations by professionals on selected topics. Student presentations of case studies and position papers. Professional portfolio creation. Critiques of peer-reviewed articles. 150 hours of experiential practice. Must enroll in the NTR 5450 course for two consecutive semesters while completing the Master of Science in Agriculture - Nutrition and Food Science Option. Corequisite(s): NTR 5600 and NTR 5610 .
courses.prerequisites: Admission into the MS in Agriculture - Nutrition and Food Science Option.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 4 units, with a maximum of 2 units per semester.

courses.title: Clinical Practice I
courses.description: Supervised pre-professional practice and on-the-job training in nutrition and dietetics. This internship course is a high-impact practice (HIP) to enhance the knowledge and application of skills of the MS in Nutrition students. Gain hands-on experience working with nutrition and dietetic companies that serve the needs of the nutrition market. An opportunity to network with the industry for future jobs. The experience must be new to the student. Students must obtain instructor/advisor/preceptor approval of the Internship experience. Periodic analysis of internship experience is reported in written journal reflections. *Students in the DI track option will take this course for 4 credits, as it serves as their ACEND required supervised practice. Non-DI track option will take this course for 2 credits. *For students enrolled in the Dietetics track option: Supervised pre-professional practice in assigned clinical, community and food service sites, minimum of 350-500 hours. *For students enrolled in the non-Dietetics track option: Supervised pre-professional practice in an internship experience identified by the student and their advisor/instructor. Corequisite(s): NTR 5450 - Current Topics in Clinical Practice I, II (2) NTR 5450 (Dietetics subplan/track/option only)*.
courses.prerequisites: Bachelor’s degree; and verification statement approved by Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND), accepted in the MS in Applied Nutrition (Blended), or accepted into CPP Dietetic Internship Program.

courses.title: Clinical Practice II
courses.description: Supervised pre-professional practice and on-the-job training in nutrition and dietetics. This internship class is a high-impact practice (HIP) to enhance the knowledge and application of skills of the MS in Applied Nutrition students. Students will get hands-on experience working with nutrition and dietetic companies that serve the needs of the nutrition market. An opportunity to network with the industry for future jobs. The experience must be new to the student. Students must obtain instructor/advisor/preceptor approval of the Internship experience. Periodic analysis of internship experience is reported in written journal reflections. Students in Dietetics Internship will take this course for 4 credits, as it serves as their ACEND required supervised practice. Non-Dietetics Internship students will take this course for 2 credits. For students enrolled in DI: Supervised pre-professional practice in assigned clinical, community and food service sites, minimum of 350-500 hours. For students enrolled in non-DI: Supervised pre-professional practice in an internship experience identified by the student and their advisor/instructor. Corequisite(s): NTR 5450 (Dietetics Internship students only).
courses.prerequisites: Bachelor’s degree; and verification statement approved by Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND), accepted in the MS in Applied Nutrition, or accepted into CPP Dietetic Internship Program.
